statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-32175 is a .NET tampering vulnerability (CWE-36, absolute path traversal): a specially crafted file can make .NET write files and directories to locations outside the intended one. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and only the Windows runtime packages (Microsoft.NetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm, win-arm64, win-x64 and win-x86) as affected, with .NET 10 fixed in 10.0.8 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/396, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/128089, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.8/10.0.8.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. They hold the .NET runtime, ASP.NET Core and SDK built for Linux on musl (the alpine.3.23-x64 and alpine.3.23-arm64 runtime identifiers). None of them contains the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime, a Windows runtime pack (no file is named for a win-x64, win-x86, win-arm64 or win-arm runtime identifier), or any native Windows PE file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. The Windows-only path handling the advisory describes is therefore not reached by any build of this owner.

CVE-2026-32175 (GHSA-rg75-q538-x34v) is a .NET tampering issue, an absolute path traversal when .NET handles crafted files, that Microsoft lists for Windows only: the advisory gives Windows as the only affected platform and lists only the Windows .NET runtime packs (Microsoft.NetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64, win-x86, win-arm64 and win-arm) as affected, up to 8.0.26 with the fix in 8.0.27 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-rg75-q538-x34v, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/396, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.27/8.0.27.md). Microsoft has not published the fix commit. DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: they hold the .NET 8 runtime, ASP.NET Core and SDK built for Alpine Linux (linux-musl), with Alpine runtime packs and no Windows runtime pack; none of them contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file, and every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. Microsoft lists no Linux runtime pack or Linux shared framework as affected, so the vulnerable code is not in the execute path of .NET running on Linux in any build of this owner.

CVE-2026-32175 (GHSA-rg75-q538-x34v) is a .NET tampering issue: .NET improperly handles specially crafted files, letting an attacker write files and directories to locations of limited choice. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform, and the only affected .NET 9 packages are the Windows runtime packs (Microsoft.NetCore.App.Runtime.win-*), fixed in 9.0.16 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-rg75-q538-x34v, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/396, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/128089, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.16/9.0.16.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build is the Linux (linux-musl) .NET runtime for x86_64 and aarch64, and none of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file, so no Windows runtime pack, which carries the native Windows runtime, is present. The flaw is in file handling that Microsoft scopes to Windows, so it is not reached by .NET running on Linux in any published build.
